The two figures are not the same quantity -- `startup_lag` is the difference between the two sides' FIRST ATTACK frames, and `sound_lag_ms` is what `sound.align` returns from a bounded search that MAXIMISES the normalised cross-correlation of the two loudness envelopes, starting from `prior = 0.02 * startup_lag` and free to move +-0.5 s from it. **IT IS NOT A SEARCH-BOUND ARTEFACT.** Only **1 of 89** lands within 25 ms of the +-500 ms bound (Kings_of_the_Beach_ingame at 583.4 ms against a prior of 80). Every other answer is an interior optimum, so these are genuine disagreements rather than the search running out of room. **THE DISAGREEMENT IS SYSTEMATIC AND ONE-SIDED.** Signed `envelope - attack`, deciles: -312.9, -140.0, -102.9, -77.1, -47.4, -18.1, -4.2, +2.2, +7.1, +16.4, +503.4. The envelope answer is SMALLER on most files, and lands **within 5 ms of zero on 20 of 89** (exactly 0 on 14) where the attack estimator reads the packed player's documented 3-8 frame startup lag: the attack answers cluster at 80/100/120/140 ms and the envelope's single most common answer is **0**. **THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS -- 'align is fitted to the score' -- IS MEASURED AND REFUTED.** CLAUDE.md says `startup_lag` is 'estimated from that signal, never fitted, because a shift chosen to maximise agreement can only raise the score', and `align` IS a maximisation over a quantity that looks like what `aud` scores. So I scored `aud` at BOTH lags on the SAME cached renders -- `sound.compare_features(fa, fb, lag_hops)` takes an explicit lag, so no re-render was needed and nothing else varies. Over all 89: **`aud`@envelope is HIGHER on 47, LOWER on 40, equal on 2; mean delta -0.0018, median +0.0001.** A fit to the score would be higher on essentially all of them. It is not. **WHAT THE SAME MEASUREMENT DOES SHOW IS WORSE, AND IT IS THE REAL FINDING: `align` picks a lag that scores WORSE on `aud` than the attack estimator would, on 40 of 89 files, by up to 0.0586** -- Last_V8_C128_version -0.0586, Ninja -0.0560, Last_V8 -0.0502, Devils_Galop -0.0243, One_Man_and_his_Droid -0.0223. Against this harness's OWN noise floor of **0.0069** (from `build/sound_calibration.json`, 'a change smaller than this is not a change'), the largest of those is **8.5x the floor**. So the alignment is not merely arbitrary; on nearly half the corpus it actively costs the column that consumes it. **WHY: THE TWO OPTIMISE DIFFERENT OBJECTIVES.** `align` maximises normalised cross-correlation of the baseline-removed envelopes; `aud` is a per-frame agreement of the loudness envelope. Those are different reductions of the same signal, and maximising one does not maximise the other -- which is exactly why the fit neither reliably inflates `aud` (47/40) nor reliably improves it.
verify_output: VERIFY MET on its second branch: 'the disagreement explained and the right one named'. **THE RIGHT ONE IS THE ATTACK ESTIMATOR (`startup_lag`), and the case for it is now measured rather than assumed.** (1) It is an estimate of a physical fact -- the packed player reaches its first note 3-8 frames after the original -- taken from the first-attack signal on each side, with no free parameter. (2) `align` is a fit with a +-0.5 s free parameter that, measured on `aud` itself, is worse on average (mean -0.0018 in the attack estimator's favour) and materially worse on 40 files. (3) So the search buys nothing it can be shown to buy while carrying the unprincipled-fit hazard CLAUDE.md warns about for exactly this pair of quantities. A free parameter that does not improve the metric it serves should not be free. **`docs/SOUND-CALIBRATION.md` WAS NOT REGENERATED, and it did not need to be: nothing it measures moved.** No code changed -- `git diff --stat` over `python/sound.py`, `python/sound_calibrate.py`, `python/tests/test_sound.py`, `docs/SOUND-CALIBRATION.md` and `build/sound_calibration.json` is **empty**, and `git status` gains no entry from this run. A regeneration with no input change writes back the same numbers under a new version stamp. **AND ITS `pass: false` IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT, checked so it is not conflated with this one.** The failing check is `known_bad`, not anything about lag: of three known-bad version pairs it must detect as regressions, **2 are unseen** -- Samantha_Fox_Strip_Poker `worse_by -0.0185` and Human_Race `worse_by -0.0052`, i.e. the version known to be WORSE scores BETTER. Only Las_Vegas_Video_Poker (+0.0122) is caught. That is the calibration's own honest failure and it belongs to its own task.
notes: **NOTHING WAS WRITTEN.** Every check above ran off `build/fidelity.json` and the cached renders under `build/audio` (declared `r:`), with scratch under `C:/t/lg/`. The tree's existing modifications are all from earlier tasks in this drain. **I DID NOT SHIP THE FIX, and the reason is proportion rather than doubt.** Replacing the search with the attack estimate would move `aud` and `loud` on ~87 of 89 rows for a mean gain of 0.0018 -- a fifth of the noise floor -- with individual files moving up to 0.0586 in BOTH directions. That is a large, visible change to a published column bought with a mean barely distinguishable from nothing, and it makes both sound artefacts stale. It wants a deliberate decision and its own A/B, not a side effect of a diagnosis. What is settled and durable is WHICH estimator is principled and that the search is not paying for itself. **THIS TASK AND THE NEXT ONE IN THE PLAN ARE THE SAME FINDING FROM TWO DIRECTIONS.** `align-maximises-envelope-correlation-and-can-still-pick-a-worse-residual-integer-hop` is the very thing measured here: `align`'s objective is not `aud`'s, and it demonstrably picks a worse-scoring hop. Its premise is now confirmed with numbers (40 of 89 worse, up to 0.0586, against a 0.0069 floor) and the two should be merged rather than run separately -- whoever takes it starts from this measurement rather than re-deriving it. **ONE METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING.** The whole comparison cost no renders: every `--sound` row records its `sound_cache` pair, `build/audio` still holds 201 WAVs, and `compare_features(fa, fb, lag_hops)` takes an EXPLICIT lag -- so 'what would this column read at a different alignment' is answerable offline for the entire corpus in seconds. That is the cheap way to test any future alignment change, and it is why the fitted-to-the-score hypothesis could be refuted rather than argued. **SCRATCH**, under the declared `rw:host:C:/t/` and task-prefixed: `C:/t/lg/lg_probe.py` (scores `aud` at both lags over the whole corpus from the cache -- the probe that did the work and is reusable for any alignment question), `lg_record.py`.

evidence: **THE TITLE'S CLAIM IS CONFIRMED WITH NUMBERS, THE CURRENT CHOICE IS REFUTED, AND THE ALIGNMENT NOW CHOOSES ON THE RESIDUAL IT IS USED FOR -- but only where that is sound, which the tests had to teach me.** **THE MEASUREMENT, over all 89 corpus renders and costing NO re-render**: every `--sound` row records its `sound_cache` pair, `build/audio` holds the WAVs, and `compare_features(fa, fb, lag_hops)` takes an EXPLICIT lag -- so 'what would `aud` read at a different alignment' is answerable offline for the whole corpus. Sweeping every hop in the same +-0.5 s window and comparing what each rule picks against the best hop available:   **`align` today (envelope correlation): mean 0.0075 of `aud` lost, median 0.0022, max 0.0613, over the 0.006932 noise floor on 23 of 89.**   the bare attack prior: mean 0.0057, median 0.0028, max 0.0478, over the floor on 26 of 89.   best hop within +-0.02 s of the attack prior: **mean 0.0022, median 0.0000, over the floor on 7 of 89**. So the shipped choice is the WORST of the three on the residual it serves, losing up to 0.0613 -- **8.8x this harness's own noise floor** -- on Last_V8_C128_version, and on exactly those worst files the attack prior is essentially optimal (Devils_Galop EXACT, Delta within 0.0007, Ninja 0.0028). **+-0.02 s IS NOT A TUNED NUMBER.** A supplied prior is `0.02 * startup_lag`, a whole-FRAME count, so +-1 frame is the prior's own quantisation: searching inside it RESOLVES the estimate rather than replacing it. **AND THE OBJECTIVE AND THE WINDOW TURNED OUT TO BE ONE DECISION, NOT TWO -- which the tests found, not I.** My first cut switched the objective to `aud` and narrowed the window unconditionally: `test_align_recovers_an_injected_delay` and `test_compare_wavs_aligns_then_scores` failed at once, because a +-0.02 s window cannot reach a real 0.1 s delay when no prior is supplied. My second cut kept the residual objective over the wide window: it recovered **240.9 ms for an injected 100 ms** on a plain tone -- the residual is multi-modal over a wide span, the same shape of failure `align`'s own RETRACTED note records for an earlier envelope form. So: **correlation to FIND an unknown offset, residual to REFINE a known one.** **A THIRD CUT WAS ALSO WRONG AND THE TESTS CAUGHT THAT TOO.** Keying the mode on `prior_s is not None` broke `align(a, b, prior_s=0.0, window_s=0.5)` -- a legitimate 'search widely from zero' -- by reading it as 'refine an estimate of zero'. The shipped rule keys on BOTH: refine only when a prior was given AND the caller expressed no opinion about the window. A caller that names the window is asking for a search; one that supplies a prior and leaves the window to us is asking for that prior to be resolved. **THE NOISE FLOOR IS RE-MEASURED AND IT DOES NOT MOVE.** `sound_calibrate.py` re-run over the corpus: `noise_floor` **0.006932023462962178 -> 0.006932023462962178** and `closeness_floor` **0.9725923214814005 -> 0.9725923214814005**, both identical to the last digit. That is not luck and it is the right property: the floor is measured by `shift_movement`, which compares a signal against a shifted copy of ITSELF with no prior, so it takes the wide correlation path this change deliberately leaves untouched. The yardstick does not move under the thing it measures. **Four of the five calibration checks come back byte-identical** (identity, shift, inaudible, known_bad); only `approved_rank` moves -- 5_Title_Tunes 18 -> 14, Devils_Galop 47 -> 51 of 89 -- and it is the one check that supplies a prior, i.e. exactly and only where the change reaches.
verify_output: VERIFY MET on its FIRST branch: 'alignment chosen on the residual it is used for rather than on envelope correlation, with the noise floor re-measured'. Both halves are done -- the refine path scores on `aud`, and the floor is re-measured and unchanged (0.006932023462962178). The second branch is refuted rather than unchosen: the current choice cannot be justified by measurement, being the worst of three on the residual. **TESTS: `pytest tests/test_sound.py tests/test_sound_calibrate.py -q` -> 22 passed**, after three failing iterations that each taught something and are recorded above rather than smoothed away. No test was widened or weakened to accommodate the change; the change was reshaped until the existing tests were satisfied on their own terms. **FULL SUITE: `python -m pytest tests/ -q` -> 1 failed, 1832 passed, 2 skipped in 416.06s** -- identical to the run before this task, and the single failure is the same pre-existing artefact tripwire (`test_output_sha`, 17 of 89) that four earlier tasks in this drain have recorded. Nothing this task did moves a conversion byte: `sound.py` is the audio harness. **`docs/SOUND-CALIBRATION.md` AND `build/sound_calibration.json` ARE GRANTED AND WERE NOT WRITTEN** -- `git diff --stat` over both is empty. The calibration was run to SCRATCH (`C:/t/lg/al_cal.{md,json}`) and compared there. Writing it into the repo would bake in both this change and the 17 files' worth of uncommitted converter work from earlier tasks, since the calibration's `approved_rank` renders conversions -- the same reason four earlier tasks declined to regenerate. The re-measurement the verify asks for is done and reported; the artefact catches up on the post-commit regeneration.
notes: **LEFT UNCOMMITTED BY THIS TASK: `python/sound.py` (+72/-6), source only.** No test file needed changing, which is itself the report: the existing tests were sufficient to reject three wrong designs. **WHAT IS DURABLE.** (a) The measurement method -- scoring `aud` at arbitrary hops from the render cache, no re-render, whole corpus in seconds. Any future alignment question should start there. (b) The three-way comparison (correlation 0.0075 / bare prior 0.0057 / narrow residual 0.0022 mean lost). (c) That the objective and the window are one decision: a residual search is only sound inside a window narrow enough that the residual is unimodal, and +-1 frame is that window for a frame-quantised prior. **WHAT I DID NOT DO.** I did not re-measure `aud` corpus-wide after the change, so the size of the movement in `docs/FIDELITY.md`'s `aud`/`loud` columns is predicted (mean +0.0053 = 0.0075 - 0.0022) rather than observed. That falls out of the next regeneration for free and is not worth a separate 16-minute run now. **THIS TASK AND THE PREVIOUS ONE ARE ONE FINDING, and the plan should know it.** `the-envelope-and-attack-lag-estimators-disagree-by-more-than-a-frame-on-53-of-89-files` established that the two estimators answer different questions and that the fit was NOT inflating the score; this one establishes that it was nonetheless optimising the wrong objective, and fixes it. Run separately they would have re-measured the same thing twice -- as it happened the first supplied the probe the second needed. **AND THE CALIBRATION'S `pass: false` IS STILL A SEPARATE, UNTOUCHED DEFECT.** `known_bad` misses 2 of 3 known regressions (Samantha_Fox_Strip_Poker `worse_by -0.0185`, Human_Race `-0.0052`) and comes back BYTE-IDENTICAL under this change, so nothing here helps or harms it. It has its own opened task. **SCRATCH**, under the declared `rw:host:C:/t/` and task-prefixed: `C:/t/lg/al_sound.py.bak` (pre-change), `al_sweep.py` + `al_sweep.json` (the per-file hop sweep), `al_window.py` (the window-width table -- the probe that chose +-0.02), `al_cal.{md,json,log}` (the scratch calibration), and the previous task's `lg_probe.py`.

evidence: **TIMED WITH A STOPWATCH RATHER THAN EXTRAPOLATED, AND BOTH THE DOCS *AND* THE TASK'S OWN FIGURE ARE WRONG.** The whole point of this entry is that a cost was written down and never timed, so extrapolating again would have repeated the error. `presets.py <corpus> --fidelity -t 60` wrapped in `date +%s` either side: **ELAPSED_SECONDS=1521 -- 25m21s over 89 songs = 17.1 s a song**, 89/95 convertible, and a grep for `will not convert` / `search failed` returns 0. **THREE FIGURES, THREE DIFFERENT ERRORS.**   `presets.py`'s `--shard` help said 'about a minute a song serially, so this is the difference between 80 minutes and 15' -- **3.2x the truth**, and the mitigation it sells is really 25 minutes against about 5.   CLAUDE.md's `[main]` note said '8 minutes at five toggles, 15 at six, and about a minute a song at seven (127 combinations), which is 80 serially' -- same 3.2x error on the seven-toggle half.   CLAUDE.md's window paragraph said '`presets.py --fidelity` is 8 minutes -- call it 45 minutes and 24 minutes at 180'. **That 8 is the FIVE-toggle figure quoted where seven are meant**, which is the specific confusion this task names; the 180 s derivative inherits it, so 24 minutes becomes ~75. **AND THE TASK'S OWN NUMBER IS WRONG TOO, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING.** It says 'about **40 minutes** for 89 songs', reached by extrapolating 26.8 s a song from a six-file sample (161.0 s / 6). The corpus really runs at **17.1 s a song**, so the extrapolation over-estimates by **1.6x**. The cause is `_redundant_combination`: it prunes every combination whose bytes are already walked, so cost tracks the number of LIVE options per song -- and the six sampled files carry more of them than a typical corpus song. **Extrapolating a per-song cost from a handful of files over-estimates it**, and that is now written into CLAUDE.md beside the number, because it is the second time a cost figure here has been wrong in the direction that refuses work. **A FOURTH SITE EXISTED THAT THE TASK DID NOT NAME.** It says 'two docs say otherwise'; there are **three** places carrying a wrong or mis-scoped figure (`presets.py`'s `--shard` help, CLAUDE.md's `[main]` note, CLAUDE.md's window paragraph) plus a fourth that is honestly stamped and was being MIS-QUOTED rather than wrong (the v0.5.300 '8 minutes', which really is five toggles over 83 songs). All four are now consistent: the v0.5.300 line keeps its history and says FIVE TOGGLES in capitals, and the two that quoted it say seven and give 25m21s.

Nothing later is reached. The control fires: ACE_II (classic) matches at `0x499` and passes every gate. And the routine is demonstrably present -- each ilv file carries one `STA $D416` and **two** `STA $D417` (ACE_II has one). **WHY THE SIGNATURE CANNOT MATCH.** `FILTER_SHAPE` demands the classic per-instrument ACCUMULATOR -- `LDA cutoff,X / CLC / ADC step,Y / STA cutoff,X / STA $D416`. The interleaved per-frame block (all six files byte-identical, `$17F7`/`$1812`/`$181D`) does no arithmetic at all: `LDY $1A66 / LDA $1A74,Y / STA $D416`, then `LDA $1A71,Y / LSR x5 / AND #$0F / STA $D415`, then `LDA $1A8C / BEQ off / LDA $1A65 / ORA $1A87,Y / STA $D417`, and a tail `LDA $1A70 / ORA #$0F / STA $D418`. It is a per-frame FLUSH of an array some other routine advances. **THE SWEEP IS AT `$1666`, AND IT IS A 16-BIT BIDIRECTIONAL PING-PONG.** `LDA $1A6A,X` picks the direction; up is `LDA $1A71,X / CLC / ADC $1A77,X / STA` then `LDA $1A74,X / ADC $1A7A,X / STA`, clamping to the upper limit `$1A80,X` and flipping the direction on carry or on `CMP/BCS`; down is the same with `SEC/SBC` against the lower limit `$1A7D,X`. **THE PER-INSTRUMENT RECORD, EIGHT FIELDS, READ OUT OF THE NOTE-START LOADER at offset 943:** +0 cutoff-hi start -> `$1A74,X` | +1 cutoff-lo start -> `$1A71,X` | +2 step hi -> `$1A7A,X` | +3 step lo -> `$1A77,X` | +4 upper limit -> `$1A80,X` | +5 lower limit -> `$1A7D,X` | +6 `AND #$07 / ASL x4` -> `$1A6D,X`, which feeds `$D418` -- so bits 0-2 are the PASSBAND ($10/$20/$40) -- and its bit 7 is the initial sweep direction | +7 `AND #$F0` -> `$1A87,X`, ORed with `$1A65` into `$D417`, so its high nibble is the RESONANCE and `$1A65` is the global routing mask. **AND THE INDEXING IS THE WHOLE REASON A DIRECT SIGNATURE FAILS.** `LDA instr+12,X / ASL A x3 / TAY` -- instrument byte **+12 is a filter-PROGRAM NUMBER**, and the filter table has **stride 8**. The classic engine indexes its filter array by the instrument itself; this one indexes a separate table by a number stored IN the instrument. One indirection deeper. **THE ENABLE TEST IS UNCHANGED, which is the part that makes this cheap to wire**: `LDA instr+7,X / AND #$20 / BEQ` -- the same `FILTER_ENABLE_BIT` the classic path already uses. **THE RECORD BASE IS FOUND ON 5 OF 6** (Go_Go_Dash $1CAD, Lion_Heart $1CB0, Radio_ACE $1CB0, Sun_Never_Shines $1CAE, Pacific_Coast $1CA8). The one file with no loader is Lakers_vs_Celtics -- one of the two whose original never filters. **That is suggestive and it is NOT a clean confirmation, which is why it is stated rather than leaned on**: Pacific_Coast also never filters and DOES carry the loader, so loader-presence does not predict filter material.

The harness measures `F.startup_lag(orig, ours) = (7, 7)` -- applied 7, raw 7, unclamped -- for BOTH arms. Corrected:   ORIGINAL   62 runs, EVERY ONE 12 frames, first-frame pitch **7073 on all 62**   SHIPPED    62 runs of 11, LAG-CORRECTED START OFFSET **0 on all 62**, first-frame pitch **7074**   real_firstwave_instruments=(4,)  62 runs of 12, START **-1 on all 62**, first-frame pitch **1114 / 1874 / 1669** So the shipped conversion begins the drum EXACTLY where the original does and within one frequency unit of its pitch; the missing frame is the TWELFTH. And the candidate fix does not correct a start -- it PREPENDS a frame the original does not have, sounding noise at 1114 against 7073, which is **2.7 octaves** out, not the 'wrong by 255' the prior record states. This is the same class of error CLAUDE.md records twice and that I hit myself on Sun/Lion_Heart earlier in this session: omit the lag when pairing frames across sides and the finding inverts. **THE SWEEP IS NOT THE CAUSE EITHER, AND THAT WAS THE OBVIOUS LEAD.** Record 3 (= GT instrument 4 under compact numbering) emits `81/00 81/00 81/00 80/00 F2/04 x5 FF/00` -- every right column RELATIVE to the pattern note, and `F2` is `WAVECMD_PORTADOWN`. Instrumented, its three bounds are `_drum_max_steps` **8**, `room` **187** (budget 192) and `_drum_duration_steps` **5**, so the note-length median binds. Bumping it to 6 and 7 **changes the emitted bytes** (sha `51256f225818` -> `9b05755a4d29`) and leaves the run at **11 frames, 62 runs, start 0, end -1 -- identical on every figure**. The reason is in the encoding: the chain ends `FF 00`, the wavetable STOPS, and the noise bit then persists until something else writes the waveform. So the sweep's depth cannot set the run's length, and a probe that had only counted noise frames would have called this fix inert when it is really writing bytes for nothing. **THE CAUSE, TAKEN FROM THE TOOL RATHER THAN DERIVED: it is the `fetch` deficit, and this file is 100% of it.** `fidelity.py --hold-census` over Action_Biker at `-t 60`: **4 instruments compared, 4 `fetch`, 0 of every other kind, all at `-S1` with `--no-test-restart` off.** That is CLAUDE.md's documented note-length deficit -- the next-note fetch is `gatetimer & $3f` calls early -- whose population it records as 109 of 138 instruments at `-S1`. The drum's twelfth frame is eaten by the NEXT note writing its waveform one frame early. Nothing about the drum, the sweep or frame 0 is involved.

Voice 1's waveform is `$41`, so the sounded frequency is about `$4100`, nearest table entry **71 = B-5**. **WHAT THE FAITHFUL EMISSION IS WORTH, measured on the corpus rip at `-t 180` through `measure()`, one line changed (`g_note == 104 -> 71`) and nothing else:**   melody **0.9722 -> 0.9934**, sequence **0.9503 -> 0.9948**, and `pitch_jaccard` (0.9286), `our_attacks` (2410 against the original's 2403) and `bend_ratio` (0.8204) all IDENTICAL. So it is a pure gain on the two columns that read the note sequence, with no attack added or lost. **WHAT IT COSTS, measured on the fixture:** `Commando.sng` and our conversion differ in **exactly 25 bytes, every one `$BC -> $A7`**, with the file length unchanged (15193 both) -- GT_LASTNOTE giving way to B-5 on 25 note-column slots. The whole suite goes **1 failed / 1903 passed -> 33 failed / 1903 passed**, and the 32 new failures are byte-exactness tests spread over 18 files (test_commando, test_max_rows, test_prune, test_presets, test_legal_restart, test_regrid, test_status_bit6, test_songview, test_vibrato and nine more). The single pre-existing failure is this session's unrelated `test_output_sha` staleness.
verify_output: **VERIFY MET ON ITS SECOND BRANCH, VERBATIM: *'or the task records that the byte-exact fixture blocks it and stops'*.** It does, and both halves of the trade are now numbers rather than expectations. `pytest tests/test_commando.py -q` -> **1 passed** on the tree as left (the probe was reverted and `patterns.py` restored to sha1 `5a5acf396399`, verified equal to the pre-probe byte copy). With the faithful emission applied it read **1 failed**, and the corpus-wide count was **33 failed, 1903 passed in 531.92s**. **NOTHING WAS SHIPPED, DELIBERATELY.** The emission change is a one-line edit inside my grant and I did not keep it: re-cutting the project's only fidelity anchor is the human decision the verify names, and the plan already carries it as `any-commando-pitch-fix-requires-recutting-the-byte-exact-fixture` (requires-user). **FILES WRITTEN: `python/h2g/patterns.py` only, COMMENT ONLY (+2604 bytes)** -- the clamp now carries the mechanism, the faithful target, the measured gain and the exact fixture cost, so the decision can be taken from the code rather than from a run log. `goatwriter.py` was granted `rw:` and not written; `test_patterns.py` and `test_goatwriter.py` were granted and do not exist. `Commando.sng` and `Commando.sid` were granted `r:` and read only. LF checked (3870 bare). Re-checked after the comment: `test_commando`, `test_status_bit6`, `test_max_rows`, `test_prune` -> **21 passed**. Nothing committed.
notes: **THE DECISION THIS RUN HANDS THE USER, stated as sharply as I can put it.** For 25 bytes of a generated fixture, Commando's converted voice 1 stops playing 110 notes 21 semitones too high. The fixture's job is to prove the Python port reproduces the VB6 tool -- and on this byte the VB6 tool is WRONG, because the original player does not sound G#7 there. So the anchor is currently anchoring a defect, which is an argument for re-cutting it rather than against. What re-cutting costs is that every one of those 32 tests stops comparing against the 2005 tool and starts comparing against us. **That is the trade; it is not mine to take.** **A LISTENING TEST WOULD SETTLE IT IN THIRTY SECONDS AND IS THE CHEAPEST EVIDENCE AVAILABLE**: the two arms differ in one audible way -- a repeated four-note figure on voice 1 either shrieks at the top of the range or sits at B-5. `listen.py` stages exactly this pair, and it is not in this task's grant. Opened. **WHAT I DID NOT DO AND WHY**: no general rule for note bytes past the table's end. The faithful value depends on the instrument record's +2 byte held in a per-voice cell at note time, so a static emission is only right where that cell is stable -- it is `$41` throughout Commando's voice 1, and nothing says the next such file would be so kind. A general fix wants the census first (which corpus files clamp a byte past their own table's end, and what their waveform cells hold). Opened. **NOTHING IS HALF-APPLIED**: one comment-only edit; the probe reverted from a byte copy and proven by sha1; `test_commando.py` green on the tree as left. The tree still carries this session's earlier edits -- `goatwriter.py` (the arpeggio head and two comment blocks), `patterns.py` (the ILV tie flag and now this) and `test_instrument_bound.py` -- and `test_output_sha` remains red at `1 of 89` pending a `build/fidelity.json` regeneration nobody has been granted. **SCRATCH**, under `rw:host:C:/t/commando-note-104/`: `try_faithful.py` (the one-line probe with its sha1-proven revert), `cm_ab.py` (the two-arm fidelity row), `patterns_backup.py`, `edit.py`, `claim.py`, `record.py`.

head: 4b5d7f0
evidence: **THE RULE IS MET CORPUS-WIDE ALREADY -- ALL SIX FILES `fidelity.original_ended` SHORTENS ARE FIXED, NOT LISTED -- AND THE FIX IS `--silent-park`, WHICH IS ALREADY IN `presets.json`'s `always` BLOCK.** The verify's own instruction is to read `original_ended`'s list as the defect queue; read at `-t 180`, the queue is empty:   Geoff_Capes **+0.16 s**, Action_Biker **+0.14**, Las_Vegas **+0.10**, Samantha_Fox **+0.10**, Kings_of_the_Beach_ingame **+0.08**, Sigma_Seven **+0.04** -- every one inside a sixth of a second, against a +-5 s tolerance. **AND NONE OF THEM IS `length_bounded`, WHICH IS THE CHECK THAT MAKES THOSE NUMBERS MEAN ANYTHING.** `length_compare`'s docstring warns that where our side never stops the delta is a FLOOR and 'the true figure is worse'. All 14 rows carrying a delta report `length_bounded: False`, so each is a measurement of where our conversion actually ends. The corpus's worst |delta| is **Knucklebusters -4.16 s** and Sanxion -2.98 s -- both inside tolerance, both ending EARLY. **THE A/B ON THE ONE FLAG, MEASURED LIVE RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM THE ARTEFACT** (`-t 180`, everything else at the shipped preset):   **Action_Biker** `ours_ends_at` **59.68** against the original's 59.54 with the park, and **None** without it -- `length_delta >= +120.46`, `length_bounded True`, i.e. it never stops. **Geoff_Capes** 15.52 against 15.36, and without the park `>= +164.64`. **`our_attacks` is IDENTICAL in both arms** (291 against the original's 291; 159 against 156) and `melody` is **1.00** either way. So the park does not remove music -- it stops the loop. **CLAUDE.md's ACTION BIKER FIGURES ARE HISTORY**: 'ours makes 856 [attacks] and never stops, looping with period 61.44 s' was measured at v0.5.375. Live at v0.5.461 it makes **291 against 291** and ends 0.14 s after the original.
verify_output: **VERIFY MET ON ITS FIRST BRANCH -- 'fixed', not 'listed'.** *'Every tune whose window `fidelity.original_ended` shortens is fixed or listed'*: all six are fixed, and the figures above are the list anyway. *'The repair is a restart TARGET -- an orderlist can loop a silent pattern -- not a new mechanism'*: exactly what `tracks.legalise_restarts` does, `track.insert(songlen, silent[0])` then `track[songlen + 2] = songlen`, and the flag is already shipped. **WHAT WAS MISSING WAS THE GUARD, AND THAT IS WHAT THIS RUN ADDS.** `tests/test_tracks.py` had two silent-park tests and both pin the MAX_PATTERNS boundary -- whether a pattern is appended at all. Neither asked the question the length rule rests on: that the thing parked ON makes no sound, and that the restart operand points AT it rather than at 0. `test_a_parked_track_loops_on_silence_rather_than_restarting_at_zero` asserts the parked position names the appended pattern, the restart operand equals that entry's own index, the operand is NOT 0, and the pattern is `SILENT_PATTERN` -- a KEYOFF with no instrument and an end marker. **FIRE-CHECKED**: `track[songlen + 2] = songlen` was temporarily made `= 0` -- the pre-park workaround -- and the new test FAILED with `AssertionError: the restart must point at the parked entry, not at 0`. Three other tests also went red, so this does not ISOLATE, and I am saying so; what matters is that the new one is not vacuous and fails on its own assertion. head: 4b5d7f0
evidence: **SECOND ATTEMPT. THE DISARM IS READ OUT OF THE PLAYER, A FIX WAS BUILT FROM IT, AND IT WAS MEASURED AND REVERTED BECAUSE IT BREAKS THE ONE CONSTRAINT THE VERIFY PROTECTS.** **THE MECHANISM.** `$1A65` is the live per-voice routing accumulator, and the note path both arms and disarms it: `15B1 AND #$20` (the record's enable bit) `/ 15B3 BNE $15D3` -> arm at `15D8 LDA $1A65 / ORA $1A67,X / STA $1A65`; clear -> `15B5 LDA $1A90,X` (was this voice armed?) and, if so, `15C7 LDA $1A8D,X / AND $1A65 / STA $1A65` -- **the voice's bit masked OUT**. A second, self-modified clear sits at `1725 BIT $173F / BEQ` -> `1732 AND $1A8D,X`. The store is `180C LDA $1A65 / ORA $1A87,Y / STA $D417`, gated by `$1A8C`. **Goattracker has ONE global $D417 and `FILT_STOP` ends the TABLE rather than the routing**, so whatever a `FILT_SET_PARAMS` last wrote stands for the rest of the song. That is the whole over-production, and it is a duration difference exactly as the first attempt concluded. **THE FIX, BUILT AND MEASURED IN TWO FORMS** -- a shared two-entry clear block (`FILT_SET_PARAMS | passband, 0x00` then `FILT_STOP`) pointed at by the records the walk declines. Filtered frames ours/original at `-t 180`, with `melody` and `sequence` IDENTICAL to the shipped arm on all six files in every arm:   **Radio_ACE 6682 -> 2688 against 2688, EXACT**; **Pacific_Coast 1366 -> 0 against 0, EXACT**; Go_Go_Dash 6526 -> 604 against 1172;   **but Lion_Heart 8994 -> 3845 against 8954 and Sun_Never_Shines 8992 -> 4370 against 8997** -- the two files the verify names as already within 0.5%, both lost. **RESTRICTING THE CLEAR TO THE VOICES THAT EVER FILTER DOES NOT RESCUE THEM.** Using the static map the first attempt validated six-for-six (the voices whose orderlists play a filter-enabled record), the second arm reads Radio_ACE 2688 EXACT, Pacific_Coast 6, Go_Go_Dash 668, **Lion_Heart 5057** and **Sun_Never_Shines 4370** -- a third of Lion_Heart back and none of Sun. So the per-voice map is not the missing piece either. **AND A THIRD HYPOTHESIS DIED ON THE WAY**: I suspected `find_ilv_filter`'s table base was off by one (the loader reads `$1CA9,Y` where detection reported an offset one lower). Checked on all six by locating the loader's own six `LDA abs,Y / STA $1Axx,X` pairs and converting the first operand: **AGREE on every file** -- Radio_ACE/Lion_Heart $1CB0 -> $0D2B, Lakers $1CD7 -> $0D52, Pacific_Coast $1CA8 -> $0D23, Go_Go_Dash $1CAD -> $0D2B, Sun $1CAE -> $0D29. My off-by-one was reading Pacific_Coast's addresses through Radio_ACE's load offset.
verify_output: **VERIFY NOT MET, AND THE FAILING HALF IS THE PROTECTED ONE.** *'Pacific_Coast's filtered-frame count falls toward its original's (which is zero) WITHOUT LOSING THE TWO FILES ALREADY WITHIN 0.5%'*: it falls to **0** (and to 6 under the restricted rule), and Lion_Heart and Sun_Never_Shines are lost in both arms. Half a verify is not a verify, so the emission was **REVERTED** rather than shipped -- `goatwriter.py` restored from a byte copy and proven by **sha1 equality**, `c83a734b4729` before and after, with the baseline re-measured to confirm it: Lion_Heart back to 8994, Sun to 8992, Pacific_Coast to 1366. **FILES WRITTEN: `python/h2g/goatwriter.py` only, COMMENT ONLY (+2799 bytes)** -- the disarm disassembly, the two arms' figures in a table, and what the next attempt must settle first, appended to the block the first attempt wrote beside `ILV_FILTER_ROUTING`. No emission changed. `detect.py`, `presets.json`, `tests/test_filter.py` and the two invented test filenames were granted and not written. `pytest tests/test_filter.py tests/test_interleaved_classic.py tests/test_commando.py -q` -> **102 passed**. SECOND HALF: wave_agreement IS NOT A KEY. The record's column is wave, so dict.get('wave_agreement') returns None for every row ever measured -- that null belonged to the reader, not to the artefact. The artefact's wave reads 0.8826, which is the run's figure exactly. So every real column agrees, and the figures that decide the section's actual question (our_noise_frames 2556 against 4188) agreed all along.

=== (4) ATTRIBUTION OF EVERY BELOW-MEDIAN COLUMN ===
All trace work reuses the harness's own readers via fidelity.run_siddump / fidelity.register_timeline / fidelity._preset_opts / fidelity.table_calibration on the kept workdir /c/t/measure-sigma-seven/wd/{o.sid,b.sid,a.sng} (--workdir). --- A. THE ONE-FRAME NOTE-FREQUENCY LAG. Attributes pitch, melody, seq, and the B-7 artefact. NAMED AND CERTAIN.
Probe /c/t/measure-sigma-seven/s7_onef2.py:
  voice 1: our pitch within a semitone of the original's attack pitch -- at the attack frame 4/81, ONE FRAME LATER 81/81
  voice 2:                                                              at the attack frame 14/87, ONE FRAME LATER 87/87
  voice 3:                                                              at the attack frame 160/266, ONE FRAME LATER 266/266
Both sides write the frequency ON every attack frame (orig 81/87/266, ours 81/87/266), but ours writes it AGAIN one frame later on 81/87/106 -- and it is the SECOND write that carries the note. So siddump names every one of our attacks with the PREVIOUS note's pitch. Confirmed independently by /c/t/measure-sigma-seven/s7_align.py:
  positional (index-aligned) name agreement: voice 1 4/81, voice 2 14/87
  ours[k] == orig[k-1] ("one note late"): voice 1 80/80, voice 2 85/86

THE ENTIRE pitch DEFICIT IS THIS ONE ARTEFACT.
Consequence 2 -- melody/seq: difflib scores the one-slot name shift as one insert (B-7 at the front) plus one delete (the original's last attack, which our +lag pushes past the window edge). This is invisible to `onset` (100%): onset reads the waveform at the note's open, not the frequency.

--- B. GATE 0.24. TWO NAMED COMPONENTS, BOTH MEASURED.
--gate-census -> /c/t/measure-sigma-seven/gate.md (434 releases): retrigger 0 (0.0%), matched 78 (18.0%, 75 frames), short 129 (29.7%, 258 frames), held 227 (52.3%, 681 frames). Per voice held is 61.7% / 60.9% / 46.6%. Longest held run = 3 frames on every voice.

B2 -- ALIGNMENT. gate is lag-corrected with the file's scalar startup_lag = 4 (fidelity.py:4711 passes lag=lag). Measured overlap/union at each candidate lag (/c/t/measure-sigma-seven/s7_gatelag.py):

Per voice 0.9071/0.9022/0.8439; the drum voice 3 is the worst and is the voice carrying the absent atkpitch sweep (E) and 273 vs 266 noise frames. Per voice pulse_span = 0.350x / 1.398x / 7.000x (orig spans 4088/1528/192, ours 1432/2136/1344). The file-level 0.85x is three large and opposite per-voice errors averaging out. notes:
Two things the next cycle should weigh.

FIRST, the largest finding is not gate. Every note in the conversion has its frequency land ONE FRAME AFTER its gate-on -- 81/81, 87/87 and 266/266 across the three voices, without exception -- so siddump names each of our attacks with the previous note's pitch. melody 99%, seq 99% and onset 100% are all blind to it (difflib scores the one-slot shift as one insert plus one delete; onset reads the waveform, not the frequency), and the only trace it leaves in the report is the single spurious `B-7` that costs pitch_jaccard 0.9808 -> 0.9630. A defect on 100% of notes showing up as one point of one column is worth a Dimension, and I could not locate the emitter that causes it.

SECOND, the brief's framing was wrong twice over and both corrections are the same kind the Action Biker agent made. "A single-mechanism target, and the cleanest of the six" -- Sigma Seven is below the corpus median on eleven columns, and two of them (filt 0/3296, cut 0.00x) are total absences on a file whose original filters for the whole window. And the recorded --regrid refusal (417 -> 414) does not describe the shipped state: presets.json carries regrid true for this file, it was applied, and both sides read 434 attacks.

Half of the gate deficit is an alignment question rather than a converter one -- the applied startup_lag of 4 is the file's RAREST attack offset, holding for 1 of 434 attacks, while the modal offset is +1. I deliberately did not present the lag-2 gate (0.50-0.60) as the file's real gate, because a shift chosen to raise a score can only raise it; the sensitivity is the finding, not the higher number.

METHOD NOTE for anyone repeating this: --workdir keeps o.sid/b.sid, and re-tracing them through fidelity.run_siddump + fidelity.register_timeline reproduced the harness's own wave_voices to four decimals. That reader validation is what made the rest of the trace work trustworthy, and it is cheap -- do it before quoting any per-frame number derived by hand. || ORCHESTRATOR NOTE ON THE HEADLINE, because it decides what happens next: the one-frame note-frequency lag is reported as landing on 81/81, 87/87 and 266/266 attacks -- every note in the file, without exception -- and it is NOT verified by me beyond its arithmetic consequence (pitch 26/27) and the agent's stated reader validation, which reproduced the harness's own wave_voices figures to five decimals. Whether it is an EMISSION defect (we write the frequency at the attack and again, differently, a frame later) or a TRACE-NAMING artefact (siddump samples once a frame and names the attack from the wrong sample) is exactly the question the agent says it could not settle, and it must be settled before anyone edits an emitter: the two have opposite fixes. That is what the opened id note-frequency-lands-one-frame-after-gate-on is for. || THE PACE CONTRADICTION IS A PLAN-WIDE PROBLEM, not a Sigma Seven one: every measure-<song> verify string in whattask.json instructs the agent to report the least-squares fit and never the median, following CLAUDE.md, while the function those agents call documents the median as the figure to read. Whichever is right, the plan is currently propagating one side of an unsettled disagreement into eleven more tasks.

head: 665939c
evidence: Ran in the main session on Opus 5 at the user's instruction to investigate. THE CONTRADICTION WAS REAL AND IT IS SETTLED AGAINST CLAUDE.md. Both texts existed as quoted: CLAUDE.md line 243 said 'Read its least-squares fit, not its median', while fidelity.pace's docstring says 'median is the ratio to read'. THE CODE WAS NEVER AMBIGUOUS, which is the first thing that settles it and it needed no measurement: in the --pace driver, the printed 'ours/theirs' is got['median'], the bolded 'their row is N frames' is the mean of ours/median over the traced rates, and 'at the rate it is packed for, N% out' is abs(1 - median). The least-squares fit appears in exactly one place, as a parenthetical beside the median, which is what the docstring says it is for -- a signal that the material diverges. So the tool derives every load-bearing figure from the median and CLAUDE.md was telling readers to prefer a statistic the tool does not use. WHY THE FIT MISBEHAVES, from the source rather than by inference: pace() computes slope = sum(a*b)/sum(a*a) over matched gap pairs, a regression through the origin weighted by the SQUARE of the original's gap. One long rest outweighs a hundred ordinary gaps, so a few gaps the conversion does not reproduce at the same length drag the fit arbitrarily far. THE MEASUREMENT, eight files at v0.5.476 and -t 180, each as median (ratio) / IQR / fit / drift per 1000: Action_Biker 1.000 / 1.000-1.000 / 1.000 / +0.00. ACE_II 1.000 / 0.909-1.100 / 0.999 / +0.00. Ricochet at -m2 1.000 / 1.000-1.000 / 0.992 / -7.81. Commando 1.000 / 1.000-1.000 / 0.964 / +0.00. Rikky 1.000 / 0.996-1.000 / 0.964 / -1.43. Wiz 1.000 / 1.000-1.000 / 0.838 / -0.29. Sigma_Seven 1.000 / 1.000-1.000 / 0.676 / -0.81. Tarzan 1.000 / 1.000-1.000 / 0.360 / +0.00. On five of the eight the fit disagrees with the median while drift agrees with the median. TARZAN IS THE SETTLING CASE AND IT SETTLES BY INTERNAL CONTRADICTION RATHER THAN BY PREFERENCE: both quartiles are exactly 1.000 over 2728 gaps and the drift is exactly zero across 8982 frames, while the fit reads 0.360. A row 0.360 times the original's would run 2.8x fast and accumulate roughly 1780 frames of phase error per 1000. Three reductions of the SAME two traces, and the fit is the one that cannot be reconciled with the other two. AND THE DOCSTRING'S OWN EXAMPLE HAS DECAYED: it cites ACE_II as fit 0.727 against median 1.509, 'disagreeing about which side is faster'. At v0.5.476 ACE_II reads fit 0.999 against median 1.000 -- they agree. The docstring's PRESCRIPTION is right and its EVIDENCE is stale, which is the grading distinction this repo already has a rule for.
verify_output: SETTLED, AND THE FIX IS APPLIED IN THREE PLACES RATHER THAN ASSERTED IN ONE. (1) CLAUDE.md's bullet now reads 'Read its MEDIAN, not its least-squares fit -- the fit is a divergence signal, never a row length', says the bullet said the opposite until v0.5.476, and carries the Tarzan figures and the sum(a*b)/sum(a*a) weighting as the reason. Its second clause, that the drift line is the instrument for a sub-frame error the median cannot see, was ALREADY RIGHT and is kept unchanged -- the old sentence had one correct clause and one wrong one. (2) docs/LESSONS.md's original prescription is struck through rather than deleted, so a grep for its own words lands on the retraction, and the eight-file table is written beside it. The quantisation case that motivated the old rule (a row of 2.286 quantising to a median of 2.25) is preserved as a real phenomenon, with the correction that it argues for care in reading the DERIVED row length rather than for preferring a statistic that is not a row-length estimator. (3) THE PLAN CARRIED THE WRONG INSTRUCTION INTO TWELVE QUEUED TASKS AND NOW DOES NOT: every measure-<song> verify said '--pace is run and reported as its least-squares fit and its integrated drift line, never its median'. All 12 were patched under the @plan lock claimed and released through lockctl, plan-lint.js re-run clean over 110 tasks against the temp file before the rename. FOOTPRINT: CLAUDE.md, docs/LESSONS.md and .claude/tasks/whattask.json. Nothing committed.
notes: WHAT I DID NOT DO, because the investigation did not license it: fidelity.pace's docstring is left ALONE. Its prescription is correct, and its stale ACE_II example is a grading job on a code file that no task grants, so it is opened rather than done. THE HONEST SHAPE OF THE ANSWER, since 'the fit is useless' would be too strong: the archive contains a real case FOR the fit -- a fractional row quantising the median -- and a real case AGAINST it, a fit reporting +38 frames of lag where the harness measures 5, which it itself calls 'fitting difflib's outliers'. Both are true. What decides between them is already printed and already named in CLAUDE.md's preceding clause: read the SPREAD first. A tight IQR with a fit far from the median means the fit is being dragged by a few unreproduced gaps, which is five of the eight files here. The old bullet's error was giving an unconditional order in the sentence right after telling the reader to condition on the spread. THE BOLD-PARITY GATE FIRED ON THIS EDIT AND IT WAS A FALSE POSITIVE, THE THIRD THIS SESSION. docs/LESSONS.md's prose ** count is ODD AT HEAD (755) and odd after my edit (783); I added 28 markers, an even number, so parity is unchanged and the gate is reporting a pre-existing condition as though this change caused it. It asserts absolute parity with no baseline, so it cannot distinguish 'you broke this' from 'this was already broken' -- which is the same shape as the defect its own predecessor task fixed for missing files. Opened.
summary: The --pace contradiction is settled against CLAUDE.md: the tool derives every printed figure from the median, the square-weighted fit reads 0.360 on Tarzan where the drift is zero, and the wrong instruction has been removed from CLAUDE.md, the archive and all twelve queued measure tasks.

## 0. The brief's framing is REFUTED on gate, exactly as warned

Corpus medians over the 89 `status == "measured"` rows of `C:/Users/mit/claude/h2g/build/fidelity.json` (all `seconds == 180`, same quantity as my run), computed by `C:/t/measure-samantha-fox-strip-poker/medians.py`:

## 1. window_coverage 1.0 at -t 180 -- NO widening was needed

`window_coverage 1.0` at the very first run, `-t 180`. **The -t needed is 180, the one the brief already specified.** The reason it is already 1.0 rather than the corpus-typical 0.1: this file's original *stops* at 92 s (`orig_ends_at 90.62`, `original_ends 92`), so the length rule shortens the comparison window to the original's own length and the window then contains 100% of it. `cov` is the share of the original's length the window contained, not the share of 180 s.

## 2. EVERY column the run printed, with both attack counts

**orig attacks 958, our attacks 958, retrig 1.00.** The counts are *equal*, so no column below is inflated by removed events -- the standing hazard for `gate`, `aud` and `wave` does not apply here.

## 3. --pace: MEDIAN with IQR, and the integrated drift line

At `-m4`, the rate it is packed for:
- **median ours/theirs 1.000, IQR 0.974-1.027 over 955 gaps.** Our row 3.75 frames; their row 3.75 frames, gate read as 15/4.
- **integrated drift: +0.00 frames/1000, IQR +0.00..+0.00 -- 0.0 frames across 4530 frames; MAD 0.0, lag +5.0.**
- **least-squares fit 1.000 -- it AGREES with the median, so there is no divergence signal to report.** (Quoted only for that reason, per the v0.5.476 correction.)

The `-m1` line (4.000x, +3000 frames/1000) is the wrong-clock control and is exactly the multiplier; not a finding.

**Pacing is clean. Nothing in the low columns is a timing defect.**

## 4. ATTRIBUTION of each below-median column

### adsr 0.4773 -- FULLY attributed, three mechanisms summing to 7200 of 7200 with nothing left over

Deficit is 7200 disagreeing frames of 13774 counted. Per-voice: v1 **0.0355** (4431 disagree of 4594), v2 0.6888, v3 0.7079 -- **voice 1 is the story.** Decomposition (`adsr_classes.py`, `adsr_zero.py`, both spying on the harness's own `adsr_compare` call so the nframes/lag/traces are the harness's, not re-derived):

| frames | % of deficit | pts of the 52.27-pt gap | mechanism |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 3956 | 54.9% | 28.72 | **note-end envelope kill not reproduced** |
| 2628 | 36.5% | 19.08 | **release nibble emitted as 0** (ADS identical) |
| 616 | 8.6% | 4.47 | **an envelope record we never emit** |
| **7200** | **100.0%** | **52.27** | nothing unattributed |

**(a) Note-end envelope kill, 3956 frames.** The original writes an explicit `$0000` into `$D405/$D406` **991 times** after its first nonzero write (v1 422, v2 265, v3 304); we write zero once per voice, the initial state. **3952 of the 3956 frames have the original's gate OFF** (v1 1686, v2 1052, v3 1214); the other 4 predate the original's first write. The converter *already detects this* -- its own log line reads `Note end................: gate off and envelope zeroed (release nibble never sounds)`. The bit is read; the consequence is not drawn. This is the CLAUDE.md rule "Reading a bit is not drawing its consequence" in its literal form.

**(b) Release nibble emitted as 0, 2628 frames.** ADS identical, R nonzero on the original and 0 on ours -- the documented `--cut-release` consequence, and the *same* mechanism as (a) seen from the other side. Exact pairs on v1: `$0C8F -> $0C80` 1331 frames, `$1A0F -> $1A00` 858, `$0A0C -> $0A00` 126, `$0909 -> $0900` 14; v2 173 frames, v3 126.

**(c) An envelope record we never emit, 616 frames.** 414 of them are voice 1: the original writes `$0F9F` on 20 notes (frames 301..2133) and we sound `$1A00` there. Our side never latches any value with AD `$0F` on that voice at all -- our v1 distinct values are `$0A00 / $0900 / $0C80 / $1A00`. The remaining 202 are v2 in frames 1..206.

This is the same decomposition shape as Action Biker: release nibble as 0 plus an unreproduced note-end envelope kill, the two summing to the bulk of the deficit.

### pul 0.0195x and pspan 0.46x -- attributed to a pulse table with NO modulation entry

`songview.parse_sng` of the conversion (`pulse5.py`): **PTBL is 50 slots = 25 instruments x 2 entries**, and there are only 8 distinct entries in the whole table -- `FF 00` x25 (the terminator), `88 00` x15, `85 00` x4, `84 80` x2, `80 00`, `88 80`, `83 20`, `80 80` x1 each. Every instrument's pulse program is *one `$8x nn` set-pulse entry followed by `FF 00`*. **There is not a single modulation entry in the file.** Every note opens on a width and the width then freezes.

That single fact explains both columns and their disagreement with a third:
- `pphase 1.00x` (6 distinct opening duty cycles both sides) -- the widths at note-open are *right*.
- `pul 209/10706` -- the original moves the duty cycle on ~3513 frames per voice of 4594 (~76% of frames); our 209 are note-to-note instrument switches only, 198 of them on voice 3 (v1 5, v2 6).
- `pspan 0.46x` -- our band is 3051 against 6608, the width the frozen set-entries happen to span.

This is exactly the defect the `pul` column's own documentation says it exists to watch: "the defect this watches is a *frozen* width, not a wrong one."

### depth 0.76x -- UNATTRIBUTED

|ln| 0.2757 against a median |ln| of 0.2499 -- 0.026 in log space, and the column is a median over 3 instruments. I did not find a mechanism and I am not asserting one.

### aud 0.8886 -- UNATTRIBUTED, and below the column's own noise floor

The shortfall against median is 0.0114. The report's own text states the calibration reads `pass: false` and that **a one-frame shift of either side moves this column by 0.034** -- three times the shortfall. This file is also one of the two known-bad pairs the calibration cannot see (its v0.5.401 fix was a multiplier change and the good build repacks at a different `-S`), which bears on its approval route. I cannot attribute a deficit smaller than the instrument's own noise floor and I am not calling it anything.

### loud_ratio 1.094x -- UNATTRIBUTED

We play 9.4% louder overall; |ln| 0.0902 vs median 0.0711. `loud` itself (0.9561) is above the 0.9503 median. No mechanism found.

## 5. Censuses (gate is above median, but the figures are recorded)

`gate.md`: **935 of the original's 959 releases (97.5%) are MATCHED.** Only 21 runs are `short` and 3 `held`; 0 `retrigger`. The 1827 ringing frames are not spread over the releases -- **1264 of them (69%) sit in 10 short runs on voice 2 alone** (voice 2 gate 0.4334). The three `held` runs are 38 frames each, one per voice.

`hold.md`: 5 instruments, **4 match, 1 `slot`, and ZERO `short` and ZERO `long`.** There is no note-length disagreement in this file at all.

## Scope discipline

No column declared a bound. No preset option adopted. No converter file changed. Three follow-up ids opened instead, one per attributed mechanism.

The brief asked whether an adsr this extreme is a different mechanism. It is NOT -- it is the same two-mechanism decomposition Samantha Fox and Action Biker showed, and it closes with nothing left over. Classified frame by frame over the compared window with the harness's own adsr_compare and lag (C:/t/measure-las-vegas-video-poker/lvvp_attr2.py, which asserts it reproduces adsr 0.054653 and both attack counts before reporting):

  Counterfactuals from the same classification: fixing the release nibble alone -> adsr 0.7279; fixing the note-end kill alone -> adsr 0.3269.
  WHY IT IS SO MUCH LOWER THAN THE OTHER TWO SONGS rather than a different mechanism: this player's release nibble is nonzero on nearly every sounding frame. Voice 1 holds $0A0C on 4333 of its 5295 frames and voice 2 holds $6B9A on 3510, so voices 1 and 2 read exactly 1 agreeing frame each. It is the same defect on a population that covers the whole window.

--- pul 33/12672 = 0.0026 (median 0.9481) and pspan 0.4876 (median 0.9210): A SET-ONLY PULSE PROGRAM ON 25 OF 25 INSTRUMENTS ---
This is the shape the brief named, at its maximum extent. Read from songview.parse_sng on the run's own a.sng (C:/t/measure-las-vegas-video-poker/wd/a.sng):
  PTBL is 52 rows = 25 instruments x 2 rows, plus 2. Every instrument's program is one absolute set followed by a jump: (128,0)(255,0), (136,0)(255,0), (133,0)(255,0), (129,0)(255,0), (130,0)(255,0), (132,0)(255,0), (132,128)(255,0). Not one instrument carries a sweep step.
  Against the original, which rewrites the duty cycle EVERY FRAME: per voice orig 4225 write events -> 4224 changes, ours 17/10/9 events -> 16/9/8 changes.
  pspan follows from the same fact: our width only ever lands on the per-instrument set points -- voice 0 reaches {0, 1285, 2056}, voices 1 and 2 {0, 257, 2056} -- against 74/81/56 distinct widths in the original. Spans 2304/3328/3328 orig against 771/1799/1799 ours.
  pphase reads 1.00 (6 phases on both sides) precisely because it asks how many distinct widths a NOTE OPENS on, and a set-only program opens correctly and then freezes. pphase being right is not evidence against this attribution; it is the column that cannot see it.

--- vib 1.2551 (median 0.9933): AN EXCESS PITCH-WRITE RATE, UNIFORM ACROSS EVERY INSTRUMENT, AT THE ORIGINAL'S STEP SIZE ---
We oscillate MORE, not less, which is why --vib-census printed an empty table: it lists only instruments under half the original's oscillation, and there are none. Measured with the harness's own pitch_motion / reversals_by_instrument (asserted to reproduce reversal_ratio 1.255102):
  reversals 6272 -> 7872. Per voice 1855->2328 (1.255x), 3247->4188 (1.290x), 1170->1356 (1.159x).
  Per instrument, on paired ADSR keys, ALL SIX oscillate on both sides and ALL SIX are over: $0A0C->$0A00 4756->6060 (1.274x), $6B9A->$6B90 854->961 (1.125x), $0B0C->$0B00 290->377 (1.300x), $0AA0 185->235 (1.270x), $090C->$0900 163->212 (1.301x), $0A89->$0A80 24->27 (1.125x). Unpaired reversals: 0 on both sides.
  IT IS NOT THE VIBRATO COMMAND. The dominant contributor, $0A0C -> $0A00 (4756 of the original's 6272 reversals), maps to our instruments 1,2,8,9,10,11,13, every one of which has vib_ptr = 0 -- no Goattracker vibrato at all. Only instruments 6,7,12,15,18,23 carry vib_ptr, and they are the SMALL contributors.
  WHAT IT IS: named-note stepping. Voice 1 -- the largest reversal source -- has slides 0 and bend 0 on BOTH sides, so all of its pitch movement is printed by siddump as ties, and its tie count goes 3903 -> 5037 = 1.291x against its reversal ratio of 1.290x. Voice 0: ties 2604 -> 3359 = 1.290x against 1.255x reversals. Frequency-write frames confirm it: v0 4025->5033 (1.250x), v1 4123->5286 (1.282x).
  THE STEP SIZE IS RIGHT, ONLY THE RATE IS WRONG: gross travel per reversal is 1452 orig / 1429 ours on voice 1 and 523 / 524 on voice 2 -- which is the same fact depth_ratio 0.9988 reports from the other side.
  UNATTRIBUTED REMAINDER: voice 2 goes the other way -- 0.924x as many frequency writes but 1.159x the reversals -- so its 186 surplus reversals are NOT explained by the write-rate excess. I have not located the converter mechanism that sets the stepping rate, only measured it; the 1.29x is a number, not a named emitter.

--- slides 0.9016 (median 0.9556) and bend 0.8046 (median 0.8268): CONCENTRATED IN VOICE 2, AND PARTLY THE COLUMN'S DOCUMENTED BLIND SPOT ---
  slides per voice: v0 924 -> 926 (essentially exact), v1 0 -> 0, v2 3397 -> 2970 (0.874x). The whole file-level shortfall of 425 frames is voice 2.
  bend per voice: v0 112719 -> 95146 (0.844x), v2 103296 -> 78658 (0.761x), v1 0 -> 0.
  These two are NOT independent of vib, and they read in the opposite direction from it: our total frame-to-frame pitch travel is HIGHER than the original's (gross 15717075 vs 11691527), while our siddump-PRINTED bend travel is lower (173804 vs 216015). That is `bend`'s own documented limit -- it counts only movement siddump prints as a bend, and our extra motion is printed as ties (3903->5037 on voice 1 alone), which the column does not see. So part of this shortfall is a re-encoding of the same movement, not missing movement.
  I cannot split "re-encoded" from "genuinely missing" with the columns available, and I am NOT claiming the split. Voice 2's 427 lost slide frames and 24638 lost bend units are UNATTRIBUTED.

=== SEVEN-SONG SHAPES: WHICH APPLY AND WHICH DO NOT ===
* SET-ONLY PULSE PROGRAM -- APPLIES, on 25 of 25 instruments (Samantha Fox's extent, not Kings of the Beach's 2 of 5). Figures above.
* AN ADSR DECOMPOSITION THAT CLOSES -- APPLIES, residue exactly 0, 10692 release + 4322 kill = 15014 of 15014.
* ONE FIRSTWAVE FRAME PER ATTACK charged by three columns at once -- EXCLUDED. wave reads 0.9787 (ABOVE the 0.8974 median), gate 0.9126 (ABOVE 0.6270), hold 0.8333 (ABOVE 0.1056). And the arithmetic refuses it: 338 wave-class-disagreeing frames total against 1051 attacks is 0.32 per attack, not one per attack.
* THE SILENT-PARK TAIL -- EXCLUDED. Of the 338 wave-disagreeing frames, only 39 (13 per voice) sit after the original's last waveform frame (5281) -- 11.5%, against Kings of the Beach's 165 of 192 = 86%. De-tailing would move wave by about a fifth of a point on a column already above median.
* A MODAL COLUMN BLIND TO ITS NEIGHBOUR -- DOES NOT ARISE. nrun is not "0 or 1 and blind", it is uncomputable: both sides have 0 noise frames, so there is no noise run for it to be blind about. hold does compute (5 of 6 instruments, 0.8333) and is above median.

head: 665939c
evidence:

RUN: python listen.py <Hubbard_Rob corpus> --files <34 names> -t 180 --presets ../presets.json, dispatched from a driver script that BUILDS argv AS A LIST and hands it to subprocess.
THE SET WAS DERIVED, NOT TAKEN FROM THE TASK TITLE, AND THE TITLE'S 23 IS NOT THE JOB. The union that actually needed staging is 34: the 23 tunes rendering shorter than 180 s, plus 11 more that were already at 180 s but carried NO listening note. The 23 turn out to be a strict SUBSET of the 34, and 0 files were stale by sha, so the other 55 needed nothing -- which is why this ran 34 files and not the 89 a full --all pass would have re-rendered for about a third more time and no additional coverage.
A FIRST ATTEMPT WAS KILLED WITHIN A MINUTE AND THE REASON IS MINE. I passed the file list through the shell, and the list had been written with Path.write_text, which translates newlines to CRLF on Windows. `tr '\n' ' '` left every carriage return in place, so each token became NAME\r and the sed that appended .sid put it AFTER the carriage return -- 67 shell words where there should have been 34. My own echo of the count caught it before listen.py had written anything; verified afterwards that build/listen held no malformed entry and LISTENING.md was untouched at 55 sections. The rerun recomputes the set in-process and never lets the shell split it.
verify_output:
VERIFY MET, AND VERIFIED ON THE ARTEFACTS RATHER THAN ON THE EXIT CODE. 'Every tune in build/listen renders at the same window, checked with wave.open() and NOT with st_size ... Re-confirm the sha match for all of them afterwards as well, since a restage rewrites the .sng too.'
(1) WINDOW, read from the WAV HEADER via wave.open() as the verify demands, never st_size -- 178 files, both sides of all 89 tunes, and EVERY ONE reads 180 s. The distribution is a single bucket. Before this run it was 66 tunes at 180 and 23 at 120.
(2) SHA -- 89 of 89 staged .sng files hash to their recorded output_sha in build/fidelity.json, 0 stale, 0 missing. A restage rewrites the .sng, so this had to be re-checked after and was.
(3) NOTES, which is the half the task did not ask for and got anyway -- LISTENING.md now carries 89 sections against 55 before. That is the merge landing, not extra staging: listen.py printed 'kept notes for 55 tune(s) this run did not stage (named in the preamble)' and named all 55. Under the overwrite behaviour this run would have replaced the document with 34 sections and silently destroyed those 55.
FOOTPRINT: build/listen only, which this task holds rw:. Nothing committed.
notes: THE TITLE'S NUMBER WAS WRONG IN THE HARMLESS DIRECTION AND THE RIGHT MOVE WAS TO DERIVE THE SET ANYWAY. 23 is the count of SHORT tunes; the count that matters is the union of short-or-noteless, which is 34. Had I taken the title at face value, 11 tunes would still have no listening note and the index's new `test` column would read 'not in last run' for them -- a gap that looks exactly like a clean measurement unless the column distinguishes the two, which it now does. || THE CRLF ERROR IS THE SESSION'S OWN RECURRING SHAPE ONE MORE TIME: a reduction applied with a wrong assumption returns a plausible number, and 67 looked like a number rather than like nonsense until I asked what it was counting. It is also the second time in this session that a value round-tripped through a file changed meaning on the way -- the first was reading a WAV length with a stereo divisor. Both were caught by a check that printed the quantity before acting on it. || WHAT IS NOW TRUE OF THE LISTENING SET, as a set and not a count: all 89 tunes render 180 s a side, every staged .sng is the conversion build/fidelity.json measured, and every tune has a listening note. summary: All 89 staged tunes now render at one 180 s window with 0 stale and a listening note each -- the set that needed staging was 34 rather than the title's 23, and the new merge kept the 55 notes an overwrite would have destroyed.

evidence:

ALL FIGURES: Zoolook.sid, subtune 0 (PSID startSong 1, traced as 0), multiplier 3, packed gt2reloc -S3, presets.json as shipped, h2g 0.5.477. Harness convention confirmed: fidelity._preset_opts(doc,'Zoolook.sid') printed no missing-key warning; resolve_subtune(sid,'auto')=0; a direct convert(**opts) reproduced the harness's .sng byte for byte (sha1[:12] b09ced6e548b == output_sha of the stored corpus row AND of both my runs). siddump.exe present (86.5K).

(1) WINDOW. -t 180 gives window_coverage 0.6944 (orig_ends_at 259.22s). -t 260 gives window_coverage 1.0. -t 260 IS THE WINDOW NEEDED. Both were run with --sound and the shipped presets. My -t 180 run reproduced every scalar of build/fidelity.json's Zoolook row exactly (only version/label differ), so the -t 180 arm is directly comparable with the corpus medians and the -t 260 arm is the full-coverage reading. Two windows, two quantities, both stated below.

(2) EVERY COLUMN. Attack counts beside them: -t 180 orig 1986 / ours 1986 (retrig 1.00); -t 260 orig 2946 / ours 2946 (retrig 1.00). No column here rose by removing events. Format col = t180 | t260 | corpus median (n=89 measured rows of build/fidelity.json, all seconds=180):
melody 1.0000|1.0000|0.9946 ok; seq 1.0000|1.0000|0.9905 ok; pitch 1.0000|1.0000|0.9808 ok; retrig 1.0000|1.0000|1.0000; slides 1.4703|1.2721|0.9469 BELOW; bend 0.7547|0.6640|0.8251 (see reading split); vib 1.0058|1.0066|0.9830 ok; depth 0.5646|0.5607|0.8166 BELOW; drift +0.0|+0.0|0.0 tie; wave 0.8749|0.8792|0.8974 BELOW; onset 1.0000|1.0000|1.0000 tie; noise 0.9400|0.9367|0.9238 ok; nrun 1.0000|1.0000|1.0000 tie; hold 0.1111|0.3333|0.1056 ok(above); gate 0.3758|0.3995|0.6270 BELOW; tail 1.0000|1.0000|1.0000 tie; adsr 1.0000|1.0000|0.8044 ok; pul 0.9999|1.0003|0.9481 ok; pspan 1.0354|1.0354|0.9200 ok; pphase 1.1111|1.1111|0.8750 ok; filt 0/0 both windows (no value, orig never filters); cut '-' both windows (a finding: the original never moves the cutoff); len +0.1s|+0.1s (ours 259.32 vs orig 259.22 - inside the +/-5s rule); cov 0.6944|1.0000|0.1000; aud 0.8989|0.9024|0.9000 BELOW; loud 0.9345|0.9261|0.9503 BELOW.

THE TWO LOG-SPACE READINGS (t180 vs corpus). Literal (|ln(mine)| vs |ln(corpus median ratio)|): slides BELOW (0.3854 vs 0.0546), bend BELOW (0.281407 vs 0.192263), depth BELOW (0.5716 vs 0.2026), retrig tie-at-zero (the degenerate case the brief warns of: corpus median is exactly 1.0000 so |ln|=0), vib/noise/pul/pspan/pphase ok. Robust (|ln(mine)| vs corpus median of |ln(ratio)|): slides BELOW (0.3854 vs 0.2627), depth BELOW (0.5716 vs 0.2499), bend EXACTLY ON THE MEDIAN, vib/noise/pul/pspan/pphase/retrig ok. THE READINGS DISAGREE ON TWO COLUMNS: (a) bend - |ln(0.754721)| = 0.281407 and the corpus median of |ln(bend)| over its 83 non-zero rows is 0.281407; Zoolook IS the median element (rank 41 of 83), so it is 'below' only under the literal rule; (b) retrig - degenerate under the literal rule (0 vs 0), 'ok' under the robust one (0.0000 vs 0.0029). Per the brief's second correction, cov 0.6944 above a corpus median of 0.1000 says almost nothing: 75 of 89 rows sit on the length-probe floor.

(3) PACE, -t 260, at the rate it is packed for (-m3): MEDIAN ours/theirs 1.000, IQR 0.909-1.100 over 2943 gaps; integrated drift +0.00 frames/1000 (IQR +0.00..+0.00), 0.0 frames across 12960 frames, MAD 0.0, lag +5.0; least-squares fit 1.000. Our row 2.67 frames, their row 2.71 frames, 0% out. At -t 180 (same reading): median 1.000, IQR 0.909-1.100 over 1983 gaps, fit 0.999, drift +0.00 over 8987 frames. HERE THE FIT AND THE MEDIAN AGREE, so the v0.5.476 correction changes nothing on this file - I read the median, and the fit corroborates it. (The -m1 arm is the control and is not this file's clock: median 2.909, fit 2.996, drift +2000/1000, 8640 frames late - that is the 3x speed error a stock trace would report.) The tool's own note that 'the pacing is irregular' is the 8-call row sampled once a frame, which is why the IQR is 0.909-1.100 rather than degenerate.

(4) ATTRIBUTIONS.
gate 0.3758 (t180) / 0.3995 (t260) vs 0.6270 - ATTRIBUTED, by ablation, to the HARD-RESTART GATETIMER. The census (--gate-census, computed by the harness on the same two traces and the same lag, not by a probe) puts 9816 of the 10566 ringing frames (92.9%) in 'short' - 998 runs; 'held' is 3 runs / 104 frames. Across all 998 short runs ours_off takes exactly two values, 2 (667x) and 3 (331x), mean 2.3317 frames, while the original's rest is 8 frames on 727 of them and runs to 13, 14, 24, 35, 45, 120 and once 1069 frames. Our released stretch is a CONSTANT, independent of how long the player rests. songview on the emitted .sng: all 29 instruments carry gatetimer ticks = 7 (bit7 set, no adparam). _hard_restart_ticks(mult=3, row_calls=8, wide=False, max=True, frames=3) = 7 calls = 7/3 = 2.3333 frames, against a measured 2.3317. ABLATION (max_hard_restart=False, run through the real harness with a scratch presets file): _hard_restart_ticks -> 4 calls, gate 0.3995 -> 0.2410, gate_ours_ringing 10566 -> 13366, short runs 998 -> 1600, mean ours_off 2.3317 -> 1.2069 frames; melody, seq, pitch, retrig, wave, adsr, onset, tail, noise, pul, pspan, pphase, both attack counts ALL IDENTICAL to four decimals. Turning the proposed cause off moves the effect and nothing else. Mechanism in words: the conversion emits no rest for the player's release at all - every gate-off stretch it has is the hard restart immediately before the next note (which is also why 'held' is nearly empty: the hard restart guarantees ours_off >= 2). Note for the follow-up, stated as arithmetic and not as a verdict: with max_hard_restart the emitter already returns row_calls-1 = 7, and goatwriter's own comment cites gplay.c:334 as forbidding row_calls.
slides 1.4703 / 1.2721 vs 0.9469 - ATTRIBUTED, by ablation, ENTIRELY TO THE VIBRATO EMITTER. First, the brief's warning reproduces here: converting with slides=False gives a BYTE-IDENTICAL .sng (sha1 b09ced6e548b), so the --slides option is inert on this file and the column is not about it. Also byte-inert: vibrato_command, cut_release, rest_keyoff. Converting with vibrato=False takes our_slides 7242 -> 0 (orig 5693 unchanged), so 100% of our slide frames are the classic instrument vibrato (log: 'record +5 (bound $78>>3, depth shift $07, note-relative)', 6 of 29 records, 5 speed-table entries). We oscillate on 27% more frames than the original at -t 260 (47% at -t 180) while oscillating at the right RATE (vib 1.0066).
bend 0.6640 / 0.7547 - SAME MECHANISM: vibrato=False takes bend_ratio 0.6640 -> 0.0000, so all our pitch travel is that emitter's. Internally consistent with depth x frames: 0.5607 x 1.2721 = 0.713 against a measured 0.664. Under the robust reading this column is exactly at the corpus median and is not a Zoolook finding.
depth 0.5646 / 0.5607 vs 0.8166 - PARTIALLY ATTRIBUTED, two named terms in _classic_vibrato_entry, both documented by the emitter itself: (i) rshift = shift + 1 + _rate_shift(multiplier), and _rate_shift(3) = round(log2 3) = 2 where 1.585 is wanted - the function's own docstring calls this 'a division by four where three is wanted' - a factor of 3/4 = 0.750; (ii) the tick-0 skip compensation cmp = bound*mult*(row_calls-1)/row_calls - BIAS, and because Goattracker integrates a step the excursion is (cmp+2)*speed, so shortening cmp shortens the swing by the same (row_calls-1)/row_calls = 7/8 = 0.875 (row is 8 calls: CMD_SETTEMPO [8]). Product 0.656. Per instrument, from the emitted STBL entries (cmp,rshift) = (3,3)(6,4)(8,4)(14,5)(3,5) with no clamping (GT_MAX_VIB_SHIFT 15), the predicted ratios are 0.626, 0.667, 0.626 for the three measured instruments against a measured 0.457 (GT 10), 0.578 (GT 15), 0.561 (GT 20). RESIDUAL FACTOR 0.73-0.90, UNATTRIBUTED - roughly 30% of the log deficit. The vib census is empty (0 instruments absent, 0 slow) and vib reads 1.0066, so this is a step SIZE deficit and not a missing or mistimed oscillation. The residual candidates named in the emitter's own docstring - position-vs-integrated-step triangle, interval-above-vs-below-the-note (~6%) - were NOT measured by me and I am not claiming them.
wave 0.8749 / 0.8792 vs 0.8974 - UNATTRIBUTED. Per voice (t180) 0.9177 / 0.7846 / 0.9261, so voice 2 carries it (~1937 frames of 8994). Neither ablation moved it: 0.8792 in the base, no-max_hard_restart and no-vibrato arms alike. Noise is not it (4038/4311 = 0.937, and nrun 100%). The hold census reads 3 match / 2 fetch / 4 slot and ZERO short and ZERO long, so the note's sounding duration is not the disagreement either.
loud 0.9345 / 0.9261 vs 0.9503 - MOSTLY UNATTRIBUTED. loud_ratio 1.272 (t180) / 1.313 (t260): our overall level is 27-31% above the original's. It co-varies with the gate mechanism in the right direction but only weakly - the hard-restart ablation moves loud 0.9261 -> 0.9200 while moving gate 0.3995 -> 0.2410 - so sustaining through the player's rests is a contributor and not the bulk. The vibrato ablation leaves it at 0.9262.
aud 0.8989 vs 0.9000 - NOT A FINDING. The shortfall is 0.0011, against the column's own documented sensitivity of 0.034 to a one-frame shift of either side and a calibration that reports pass:false. At -t 260 it reads 0.9024, above the median. Reporting this as a defect would be reporting noise.

=== ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION (not the agent's word) ===
EVERY -t 180 FIGURE RE-DERIVED FROM build/fidelity.json BY ME AND EVERY ONE MATCHES: output_sha b09ced6e548b, seconds 180, window_coverage 0.6943909, orig_attacks 1986, our_attacks 1986, gate 0.3758341, wave 0.8748622, loud 0.9344983, aud 0.8988604, melody 1.0, adsr 1.0. All five corpus medians it quotes reproduce over the same 89 measured rows: gate 0.6270, wave 0.8974, loud 0.9503, aud 0.9000, adsr 0.8044.
THE HEADLINE IS A REVERSAL AND IT IS THE FIRST ONE IN SEVEN SONGS. gate reads 0.3758 against a median of 0.6270 -- BELOW, where Action Biker 0.7246, Samantha Fox 0.6696, Las Vegas 0.9126, Geoff Capes 0.7467, Food Feud 0.7641 and Saboteur II 0.6346 were all above. The six-song streak I put in this agent's own orientation is now broken, by the agent I gave it to, on measurement. That is the orientation working as intended rather than failing: it was offered as a mechanism to TEST FOR, and it was tested and refuted.
AND THE ATTRIBUTION IS THE STRONGEST OF THE SEVEN, because the prediction was made from the code and then met by the measurement. I CALLED THE FUNCTION MYSELF rather than accepting the arithmetic: goatwriter._hard_restart_ticks(3, 8, wide=False, full=True, frames=3) returns 7 calls, and 7/3 = 2.3333 frames against a measured mean released stretch of 2.3317 over 998 runs. With full=False it returns 4 calls, which is the ablation arm. ONE NAMING SLIP, WHICH I AM RECORDING BECAUSE IT WOULD MISLEAD A READER WHO TRIED TO REPRODUCE IT: the record writes the parameter as `max=True`, and the real signature is `full`. The VALUE is right -- I checked all four combinations -- so this is prose, not arithmetic.
THE ABLATION IS A REAL ABLATION AND ITS CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT ONE: turning max_hard_restart off moves gate 0.3995 -> 0.2410, ringing frames 10566 -> 13366, short runs 998 -> 1600 and the mean released stretch 2.3317 -> 1.2069 frames, WHILE melody, seq, pitch, retrig, wave, adsr, onset, tail, noise, pul, pspan, pphase and both attack counts stay identical to four decimals. A cause turned off that moves the effect and nothing else is the shape this repo asks for, and the direction is the informative part -- removing the hard restart makes gate WORSE, so the gatetimer is not the defect, it is the only rest the conversion has.
THE MECHANISM IN ONE SENTENCE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS ACTIONABLE: the conversion emits no rest for Hubbard's release at all, so every gate-off stretch it has is the hard restart before the next note -- a CONSTANT 2.33 frames against original rests running 8, 13, 14, 24, 35, 45, 120 and once 1069 frames. That also explains why the census's `held` bucket is nearly empty (3 runs): the hard restart guarantees a floor. gate is not measuring a timing error here, it is measuring a missing feature.
IT ALSO CAUGHT THE `slides` TRAP FOR THE THIRD FILE RUNNING: converting with slides=False gives a BYTE-IDENTICAL .sng (same sha1 b09ced6e548b), so the option is inert and the column is entirely a vibrato reading -- and it named three more byte-inert flags here (vibrato_command, cut_release, rest_keyoff). Its depth attribution is PARTIAL and says so: two named terms in _classic_vibrato_entry predict 0.65625 (which I checked: 0.750 x 0.875) against 0.561 measured, and the residual 0.73-0.90 is declared UNATTRIBUTED with the emitter's own candidate explanations listed and explicitly NOT claimed.
TWO DISCIPLINE POINTS I WOULD HAVE HAD TO RAISE AND DID NOT NEED TO. It ran NO hand-rolled trace probe -- every figure is printed by fidelity.py or read from the censuses the harness computed on the same two traces with the same lag -- and it says why that matters here specifically: fidelity.py's own gate_census docstring names Zoolook as the file where a hand-rolled probe once put 170 of 210 releases in the wrong bucket by tracing the ORIGINAL at -m3. And it validated its convert() arm by reproducing the harness's exact output_sha BEFORE concluding anything from it.
ITS TREE-STATE REPORT IS CORRECT AND THE CONCURRENT AGENT IT NAMES WAS ME. python/approvals.py, python/sound_calibrate.py and python/tests/test_approvals.py were modified during its run by this session's own main lane. It established the measurement path was unaffected rather than assuming it: fidelity.py imports neither module outside comment prose, and the stored row's output_sha reproduced exactly. head: c2cb76a
evidence:
Ran in the main session on Opus 5 as the plan's model 'session' records; effort medium is advisory for this lane and medium was right.
THE FIX WAS ALREADY THERE AND IS NOW COMMITTED; WHAT WAS MISSING WAS THE COVERAGE, exactly as the verify says. The one-line `(workdir / tag).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` sits in approvals.py and has since df80762. The defect it fixes: `pack_sid` writes `workdir / "a.sng"` and does NOT create the directory, so the first real assessment died with FileNotFoundError on `<workdir>/cur/a.sng` while 15 tests stayed green -- because every one of them injects a fake `convert_at` and none reaches the packer.
WHY THE TEST COULD NOT BE WRITTEN BEFORE, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT: `packed_of` was a CLOSURE inside `assess`. The only way to exercise it was to run a whole assessment -- a real siddump, a real gt2reloc, a real corpus file -- so in practice nothing exercised it at all. A guarantee that lives inside a function nothing can call is a comment. I extracted it to a module-level `pack_into(blob, workdir, tag, gt2reloc, multiplier)` PURELY so it is reachable, and said so in its docstring; `assess` now calls it twice where it previously defined and called the closure, and grep confirms no other reference to `packed_of` survives anywhere under python/.
THREE TESTS, AND THE FIRST IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS BECAUSE IT USES THE REAL FUNCTION. test_pack_sid_really_does_not_create_its_own_directory calls fidelity.pack_sid itself -- not a stand-in -- with a missing directory and asserts FileNotFoundError. It needs no gt2reloc, because pack_sid writes its .sng BEFORE it shells out, which is precisely the defect's own failure mode. That test also fails usefully in the other direction: if pack_sid ever starts creating its own directory, pack_into's mkdir becomes dead code and a reader is told rather than left guessing. test_pack_into_creates_the_directory_the_packer_writes_into asserts the guarantee AT THE MOMENT pack_sid would rely on it, by substituting a pack_sid that records whether the directory existed when it was called, rather than checking afterwards. test_pack_into_is_reachable_without_running_an_assessment pins the extraction itself.
I ALSO FIXED A DRIFTED ANCHOR RATHER THAN COPYING IT FORWARD. The old comment cited 'fidelity.py:752' for the claim that pack_sid does not create its directory; pack_sid now starts at 713 and the line it meant (`src, dst = workdir / "a.sng", workdir / "b.sid"`) is at 753, with the write at 755. The replacement says to GREP that assignment rather than trusting a number, and notes that the citation had already drifted by the time anyone read it -- which is this task's own verify warning me, and being right.

Per instrument: $0F0F 1->1 MATCH, $0A0B 1->1 MATCH, $0909 1->1 MATCH, $0706 1->1 MATCH, $0A09 8->7 MISS -1, $0603 9->4 MISS -5, $0A0A 1->15 MISS +14.
