verify_output:
THEY PART COMPANY, on every file including the one that opened this. Across the 4 files there are 12 nrun instruments; hold's -1 reaches nrun on exactly 2 of them.

One -1 does NOT account for all three columns anywhere:
- Geoff_Capes, the file the coincidence came from, already splits internally: both its nrun instruments ($050A and $0A09) are hold-census rows reading delta -1, yet nrun MATCHES on $050A and misses on $0A09. And its noise -24 is -84 + 60, two unrelated movements.
- Confuzion: hold unanimously -1, nrun has no population at all, noise -491 from re-gating a continuous noise voice.
- Zoolook: hold mixed (delta -1 on 8 of 9, split fetch/slot by slot_delta), nrun 1.000, noise -199 from 199 fewer single-frame ticks.
- Rasputin: hold -1 on 7 of 10, nrun 4/7 with misses of -1, -5 and +14, noise -591.

WHY they move together on some files and not others -- the discriminator, and it is exact on all 12 instruments:
nrun can only see hold's -1 when the ORIGINAL's modal noise run equals the original's modal held note length, i.e. when the noise IS the note rather than an attack tick inside it.
  orig_run == orig_held (2 cases): Geoff $0A09 (12==12) and Rasputin $0A09 (8==8). Both miss by exactly -1, both have hold delta -1. 2/2.
  orig_run != orig_held (10 cases): 8 match (blind -- the run is a 1- or 2-frame tick and cannot lose a frame; a -1 would delete it) and 2 miss by something that is not -1 at all (Rasputin $0603 -5, $0A0A +14). 10/10.
12/12 consistent. Zoolook's nrun reads 1.000 not because its note lengths agree but because all three of its noise runs are length 1 and are structurally immune to a one-frame shortening -- while the same instruments lose 199 noise frames that the noise column does see. nrun compares LENGTHS, noise compares COUNTS, and when every run is length 1 nrun is blind to everything noise reads.

The reason the two are related at all: OUR noise run is the note. Wherever we sound noise for more than a tick, our modal noise run equals our modal held length exactly -- Geoff $0A09 11==11, Confuzion 11 and 23 == held 11 and 23, Rasputin $0A09 7==7, $0603 4==4, $0A0A 15==15. The original does not do this; its runs vary (Rasputin $0A09 spreads 8/9/10/11/12, $0A0A from 1 to 174). So hold's -1 propagates into our noise run length always, but only becomes an nrun MISS OF -1 when the original happened to sit at the same place.

NOT claimed: nothing here is a claim about the packed player and the -1 is not called a bound.

THE GATE IS ONE BYTE, NAMED AND VERIFIED BY ME. python/h2g/goatwriter.py:360 `FIRSTWAVE_TESTBIT = 0x09`, emitted at goatwriter.py:3263-3268 as byte +8 of every 25-byte instrument record: `((data[base+2] | 0x01) & 0xFF) if use_real_firstwave else FIRSTWAVE_TESTBIT`, where `use_real_firstwave = no_test_restart or gt_number in real_firstwave_instruments` -- both False on all three files. I read both lines from disk and they are exactly as quoted. songview.parse_sng over the emitted .sng confirms firstwave $09 on every instrument of Geoff_Capes (21) and Rasputin (14).
WHY THE RUN ENDS THERE, READ OFF THE FRAMES RATHER THAN INFERRED. Rasputin $0A09, slot 12, $D404 per frame, attack marked |:
  ORIGINAL frames 21..36  `40 40 |81 81 80 80 80 80 80 80 80 80 80 80| 41 41`
  OURS     frames 29..44  `40 09 |81 81 80 80 80 80 80 80 80 80 80 09| 41 41`
Ours spends the LAST frame of the slot on $09. Being below $10 it carries no waveform bit at all, so it simultaneously breaks `noise_runs`' `wf & WF_NOISE` walk AND `sound_note_runs`' `wf[a+held] & 0xF0` walk. ONE BYTE, TWO WALKS, SAME FRAME -- which is why the two distributions are IDENTICAL rather than merely close.
AND THE MATCH IS STRONGER THAN THE VERIFY CLAIMED: not modal agreement but IDENTICAL MULTISETS, bin for bin and count for count. Confuzion $0300 runs [[11,166],[23,198]] == hold [[11,166],[23,198]]; $0900 [[11,55],[23,66]] == same; Geoff_Capes $0A09 [[5,2],[11,21],[23,1]] == same; Rasputin $0A09 [[7,126],[9,85],[11,23]] == same; $0603 [[3,126],[4,160],[5,32]] == same.
THE WAVETABLES RULE OUT THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS. 'Our wavetable restarts at every note' is NOT the mechanism: every instrument measured ENDS ITS PROGRAM ON NOISE and never deselects it -- Rasputin instr 4 is 81 81 81 81 80 then eight `F2 04` command entries (which do not touch $D404) then `FF 00`; instr 6 is 81 81 81 81 80 `FF 00`; Geoff instr 4 is 81 81 81 80 80 `FF $13`, a jump BACK onto two noise entries. Nothing in the program ends the run; only the $09 does.
THE COUNTEREXAMPLE PROVES IT FROM THE OTHER SIDE, which is what turns this from a correlation into a rule: Geoff instr 13 ($050A) is `41 81 81 40 F2 F2 FF 00` -- its program DOES select a non-noise waveform after two noise entries -- and that is exactly the instrument where our run is 2 while our hold is 11. Command $09, `CMD_SETPULSEPTR` (python/h2g/patterns.py:143, which I read from disk and it is exactly `CMD_SETPULSEPTR = 9`), on the note row, data byte = a 1-based pulse-table entry index. Tick-0 commands run AFTER the new-note init, so the command BEATS the instrument's own pointer load. The pulse table then carries one entry point per distinct (width, direction): a `(0x80 | width>>8, width & 0xFF)` set-width row, a ramp of `(ticks, +/-speed)` rows, and `(0xFF, head)` into a shared alternating loop. Cost: a pattern reached at two different phases must be CLONED.
AND IT IS SHIPPED, OFF BY DEFAULT, as `convert(pulse_phase=...)` / `--pulse-phase`.

head: 24b9f1d
evidence:
THE MECHANISM IS LOCATED AND IT IS UNTHREADED PLUMBING, NOT A MISSING FEATURE -- which changes what this task is, because the title reads as if a measurement has to be invented.
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: `listen.render_sidplayfp(sid, out, seconds, subtune, exe=SIDPLAYFP, **mute: tuple = ()**)` at listen.py:128-129, implemented at :151-158 as `-u<n>` flags -- 'mutes a voice, 1-based like -o' -- built with `mutes = [f"-u{v}" for v in mute]` and spliced into the argv. listen.py's own `Choice` lambdas thread it (`lambda s, o, sec, sub, mute=(): render_sidplayfp(..., mute)` at :203-204), and the sid2wav fallback explicitly REFUSES it (`not mute and render(...)` at :210-211), which is where listen.py's '(choice.engine cannot mute)' message comes from. So the renderer can already do this and one engine already declares that it cannot.
WHAT IS MISSING, precisely three things:
  1. **python/sound.py threads `mute` NOWHERE** -- grep returns zero occurrences in the whole file.
  2. `sound.render_cached(sid, seconds, subtune, tag, cache, renderer)` neither accepts a mute set nor forwards one: its call is `renderer(Path(sid), out, seconds, subtune)`, four arguments, so even a renderer that supports muting is never asked to.
  3. `python/fidelity.py` never asks for a per-voice reading -- `aud` comes from a single `sound.compare_sids(...)` at fidelity.py:4978 over two whole renders, and `aud_voices` appears nowhere in the file.
**THE HAZARD THAT WOULD MAKE THIS SILENTLY VACUOUS, and it is the thing worth handing forward.** `render_cached`'s cache filename is `f"{tag}.{content_key(sid)}.s{subtune}.t{seconds}.wav"` (sound.py:389), where `content_key` is sha1[:12] of the file's BYTES. The mute set is not in that key. So an implementer who adds a `mute` parameter to `render_cached` and forgets the filename gets: the first muted render writes the file, and every later mute of the SAME BYTES returns that same cached WAV. All three 'per-voice' renders would be whichever voice was muted first, and `aud_voices` would come back as three identical numbers -- a well-formed measurement of one thing repeated, which no schema and no test of the column's shape would reject. That is this session's recurring failure waiting in a one-line omission.
COST, so nobody discovers it mid-run: `aud` currently needs 2 renders per file (both sides). Per-voice needs 3 per side, so 6 per file -- **+4 renders x 89 files, about 356 extra renders**, and the content cache cannot absorb them because each is a distinct mute set.

evidence:
RE-MEASURED AT -t 180, BOTH ARMS, CAPTURED FROM THE HARNESS'S OWN `compare` CALL so the subtune, multiplier, startup lag and tempo mode were never re-derived. Arm A is the shipped preset (`regrid: false`, an explicit recorded refusal); arm B is the same preset with regrid forced True.
  melody     A 0.994977   B 0.986312   ->  **-0.8665 pp**  (the refusal was recorded on -2.88 pp)
  sequence   A 0.996022   B 0.990015   ->  -0.6007 pp
THE NAMING CENSUS, taken from `fidelity.naming_split` as the verify instructs rather than re-derived:
  loss 0.008665 | recovered 0.010081 | **naming_share 1.1634** | melody_repaired **0.996393**
  renames 9, rename_semitones **[-1]** -- every single one exactly one semitone down
  rename_pairs (A#4->A-4) x4, (D-5->C#5) x2, (G-5->F#5) x2, (C-4->B-3) x1
So the melody loss is **116% naming**, and `melody_repaired` (0.996393) is HIGHER than arm A itself (0.994977) -- substituting the names back does not merely recover the loss, it puts regrid ABOVE the refusal. The earlier figure was 94% naming; it is more naming now, not less.
AND THE COLUMNS THE REFUSAL NEVER LOOKED AT ARE WHERE THE CASE ACTUALLY IS. I read the agreement next to both sides' note counts, per CLAUDE.md, and that is what settled it:
  orig_attacks     1252 both arms
  our_attacks      A **1262** (TEN SURPLUS)   B **1251** (one short)
  retrigger_ratio  A 1.00799                  B **0.99920**
  drift_per_1000   A **-7.8157**              B **+0.9862**
regrid is a ROW-GRID change, so drift is the column it exists to move, and it moves it from -7.82 to essentially zero -- an 8.8-point swing per 1000 frames. Meanwhile our attack count goes from ten MORE than the original to one fewer. CLAUDE.md warns that 'a change that removes the events a column scores will always appear to improve it'; here the direction is the reverse -- regrid brings our count TOWARD the original's, so melody is not being inflated by having less to score.

        3492  both gates OFF, only AD/S differ            inaudible
        2499  both gates ON, only the release differs     inaudible until gate-off, which cut_release silences
         627  gate states disagree                        `gate`'s frames, not this column's

head: 24b9f1d
evidence:
THE RULE, AND WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ONE RATHER THAN A FLATTERING ONE. A Goattracker voice keeps its last waveform selected when the gate drops -- every voice, always -- and our silent park holds one at the end of a tune; Hubbard's players write $D404 = $00 there. `wave` compared the select nibble and charged every such frame as a wrong timbre. But a latched waveform under a closed gate SOUNDS only while its release runs, and the release time is a property of the SR nibble we wrote, which the harness already has in `adsr_events`. So the exclusion is not 'frames after the original ends' (the verify's own de-tailing, which would also have dropped the frames where our release is still audibly ringing against the original's silence -- Trans-Atlantic's `$0AF8` shape, the case wave_compare's docstring was written for); it is: the original selects no waveform, both gates are off, and our release has run out. `SID_RELEASE_MS` (6, 24, 48 ... 24000 from the datasheet's rate table) -> `_release_frames(nibble)`, rounded UP and never 0, so the frame the gate drops on is always charged.
IN `wave_compare`: our gate's frames-since-drop are tracked per voice; a frame meeting the three conditions is counted in `wave_tail_frames` (row and per voice) instead of the denominator. The Dimension entry states it, so 'What this run compared' in every report carries the blindness, and `test_the_wave_dimension_declares_the_tail_rule` pins that.
THE POPULATION, CHECKED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BELIEVED, exactly as the verify demanded: the rule can only bite where the original drops the waveform, so the population is the tunes that END inside the window -- the 14 `measured` rows with `window_coverage_bounded` false -- plus Sanxion, the file the verify names as the control. Baseline rows taken with the unmodified harness, then the same 15 files through the modified one with `--baseline` (converter bytes identical on all 15, `sha-equal True` every row):
  Kings_of_the_Beach_ingame   wave 0.8477 -> 0.9435   tail 120 frames   (1062 scored)
  Las_Vegas_Video_Poker       wave 0.9696 -> 0.9811   tail 189 frames   (15843 scored)
  Sanxion                     0.6781 -> 0.6781        tail 0   -- the verify's exclusion holds
  the other 12                unmoved, tail 0 on every one
Two of fifteen move, both up, nothing else moves, and every other column is a `.` on all fifteen. KotB reads 0.9435 rather than the verify's 0.9738 because the verify's figure dropped all 165 post-end frames; this rule keeps 45 of them, where our park's release had not yet expired by the SID's own clock. That is the difference between 'after the tune ends' and 'silent', and the smaller number is the honest one.
TESTS, four, in tests/test_fidelity.py beside the other wave tests: the KotB shape (orig drops to $00 at frame 10, ours holds $40 gated off, release 0: 11 frames scored, 19 tail, wave 10/11); release F charges all 30 and release 4 (114 ms = 6 frames) charges through frame 15 exactly; the rule needs both gates off AND the original silent (our gate up -> charged in full; the original on another class -> a wrong class, not a tail; both silent -> left out as before, not counted as tail); and the Dimension text. `tests/test_fidelity.py` 207 passed; full suite 2061 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed -- the same two tree failures as before this cycle (`test_output_sha` 15 disagreeing, the LESSONS.md regrid figure).

Food_Feud.sid (m3): 7/10 records are kind='slot' with slot_delta=-1 (one at -6), 2 are kind='match'.

Ran C:\t\multiplier-does-not-explain-\probe_tempo_trunc.py against python/h2g (h2g.sidfile.load_sid, h2g.detect.detect, h2g.goatwriter.derived_group_tempos/effective_frames/recommended_multiplier/pack_subtune) over the corpus copy at r:C:/Users/mit/claude/c64server/SIDM2/SID/Hubbard_Rob:

  Battle_of_Britain.sid: multiplier=2, effective_frames=2 (int), CMD_SETTEMPO value=4.  4 % 2 == 0.
  Food_Feud.sid:         multiplier=3, effective_frames=8/3 (Fraction), CMD_SETTEMPO value=8.  8 % 3 == 2.

Wavetable/pulse-program bytes were checked (patterns.build_speed_table, scale_portamento_data, and goatwriter._pulse_tri_program) and ruled out -- none of them determines a note's slot (frames to next attack); only CMD_SETTEMPO's operand (goatwriter.tempo_command_value, goatwriter.py:2967-2995) does, since it sets how many player calls one Goattracker row lasts.

Read C:/Users/mit/Downloads/GoatTracker_2.77/src/greloc.c:1606-1697 (gt2reloc's packed-SID header writer): it arms the CIA at `0x4cc7/multiplier` (PAL), which fires the play routine exactly `multiplier` times per real 50Hz frame at a fixed, evenly-spaced period -- unrelated to where a Goattracker row boundary falls. So "one frame" in any multiplier trace (siddump-rt's -m<n>, or hardware) is exactly `multiplier` consecutive play calls, sampled once at the end of the group.

Mechanism: tempo_command_value computes CMD_SETTEMPO's operand as `int(f * multiplier)` (the row length in calls) with no constraint that it be a multiple of `multiplier`. When it is (Battle_of_Britain, 4 % 2 == 0) every row boundary lands on a frame-group boundary, so the new note's init call is always the group's first call and the previous note's last frame is sampled intact -- slot_delta is 0 on all 13 instruments, the only disagreement is the known one-call-early `fetch` artifact (gplay.c:905, unrelated to multiplier). When it is not (Food_Feud, 8 % 3 == 2, gcd(8,3)=1) the row boundary's phase within its 3-call frame group advances by 2 every row and cycles through every phase 0,2,1 -- so on 2 of 3 rows the new note's init call is NOT the group's first call, meaning it is preceded within the SAME sampled frame by 1-2 calls still holding the OLD note. The trace samples the group's FINAL state, so that frame reads as the new note and the old note's rightful last frame of held sound is invisible to any once-per-frame reduction -- exactly what fidelity.classify_hold (fidelity.py:2980-3033) reads as `slot` (the slot itself moved) rather than `fetch` (only the held length inside an unchanged slot moved).

Corpus-wide falsification check (C:\t\multiplier-does-not-explain-\probe_corpus_align.py, over the same fresh fidelity.json's 49 multi-speed rows): computed `tempo % multiplier` per file via derived_group_tempos. 14/49 files are aligned (tempo % multiplier == 0): 11 of 14 read exactly 0.0% slot. The 35 misaligned files average 26.0% slot share.

  C:\t\multiplier-does-not-explain-\probe_corpus_align.py
  C:\t\multiplier-does-not-explain-\slot_mechanism_findings.md (full writeup with the fix sketch)
